rounds.text: Chembond Chemicals Ltd trades at an attractive valuation with a price-to-earnings ratio of 16.6x [E1], backed by a rules-based screen score of 96 out of 100 pointing to high confidence [E47]. The intrinsic value calculated by a discounted cash flow model sits at Rs 346 per share, offering a notable margin of safety of 31.5% against the current market price of Rs 237 [E31, E32]. Fundamental quality shines through robust return metrics, including a trailing return on capital employed of 23.6% [E6] and a return on equity of 17.7% [E7], supported by a completely debt-free balance sheet with a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.00x [E24]. Growth momentum is robust, evidenced by trailing twelve-month sales growth of 18% [E9], profit growth of 20% [E11], and strong institutional money flow showing a holding change increase of 0.58 percentage points [E30]. Management highlights strong sales pipelines across all business units [E60], including anticipated volume growth of 15% to 20% in construction chemicals [E58] and roughly 10% in water chemicals [E59] for the upcoming quarter. Conceded: compounded sales growth over a 3-year period stands at -10% [E8], and cash conversion is currently weak at 0.23x of reported profit [E20].

The bull highlights an attractive P/E of 16.6x and a DCF intrinsic value of Rs 346 offering a 31.5% margin of safety [E1, E31, E32], but concedes poor 3-year compounded sales growth of -10% alongside weak cash conversion at 0.23x of profit [E8, E20]. Conceded: the rules-based screen scores 96 out of 100 with strong TTM sales and profit growth [E9, E11, E47], yet this masks a severe disconnect where operating cash flow reached only 46% of operating profit in March 2026 [E23]. While the bull points to a debt-free balance sheet and high ROCE of 23.6% [E6, E24], profits are running far ahead of cash due to receivables and accruals [E20], leaving operating cash flow at a meager Rs 8 Crore and free cash flow at just Rs 1 Crore [E21, E22]. Furthermore, management admits that earnings profitability presents a challenge alongside an immediate 3% margin impact from volatile metal input costs [E65, E66]. The bull leans heavily on anticipated volume growth in construction and water chemicals [E58, E59], ignoring that 30% of the water business relies on public sector clients who are refusing to amend contract terms during cost increases and rejected force majeure declarations [E72, E73].

evidence.fact: Management stated that all business units have strong sales pipelines and a positive sales growth outlook.
evidence.quote: All of these businesses are having strong sales pipelines and we see that the sales growth outlook looks positive across all these business units.

evidence.fact: Chembond is experiencing significant growth in sealants and plans to consolidate its market presence through polysulfide and PU sealants.
evidence.quote: Sealants, we are seeing a significant growth and we intend to consolidate our presence in that segment through our polysulfide and PU sealants.

evidence.fact: Capex for the year reached around 21 crores, reflecting the full year impact of the demerger, office building renovation, and property, plant, and equipment added to the books.
evidence.quote: And of course, the office building, the improvements that we've done and the The entire renovation of the office building to house our teams, so that has taken up, but twenty-one crores, whole demerger, yeah, P.P.E. which has come into our books, so this is the demerger effect.

evidence.fact: The company invested ₹90.76 lakhs during FY 2025-26 to install the solar renewable energy plant at Dudhwada.
evidence.quote: ₹90.76 lakhs were invested towards installation of the 350 kVA solar renewable energy plant at the Dudhwada, Gujarat manufacturing site during FY 2025-26.

evidence.fact: Material costs began rising from late February and March due to volatility in metal-based key inputs like zinc and molybdenum.
evidence.quote: Material costs started increasing from March, end of Feb, March. A lot of volatility in metals before that. So some key materials that we use are based on metals, so zinc and molybdenum and stuff like that.

evidence.fact: Chembond experienced an immediate monthly impact of about 3% on margins due to elevated raw material costs.
evidence.quote: But in the immediate month, we saw about a 3% impact on our margins due to these haywire costs.

evidence.fact: Management noted that while the revenue outlook remains positive, earnings profitability presents a challenge.
evidence.quote: Revenue outlook continues to remain positive. However, on the earnings, profitability is a little bit of a challenge right now.

evidence.quote: So we are starting this financial year with a strong order book for our chemicals business also.

evidence.quote: So 50% increase in terms of volume for our water business and most of this is carrying forward.

evidence.fact: The company intends to deploy some of its cash balance towards network growth and geographical expansion.
evidence.quote: We intend to deploy some of it in network growth and geographical expansion.

evidence.quote: We are maintaining a tight credit policy and our day sales outstanding for construction chemicals is around 88 days as on 31st of March 2026.

evidence.quote: The Board has recommended a final dividend of ₹1.25 (Rupee One and Paise Twenty-Five only) per equity share of ₹5 (Rupees Five only) each, aggregating to ₹336.20 lakhs for the financial year ended March 31, 2026.

evidence.quote: About 30 percent of our total business in the water business comes from public sector units, and none of them had accepted a force majeure until the government just declared it two weeks ago.

evidence.quote: Public sector is a different story. They are refusing to amend the terms. And for that, then our only hope is that the situation starts getting better.
